annotations.title: Get an upload link for artwork

description: For a client that holds the file (Claude Code, Cursor, a script): returns a signed upload_url to PUT the file's bytes to, and an upload_id for attach_artwork. target says where it goes: a cart line (line_id from get_cart), a saved quote's line (line_id from get_quote) or an order job (item_id from get_order), plus design (1 to N, on a job with several designs) and side (front or back). Give the file name with its extension (pdf is best; ai, eps, psd, jpg, png and tif are accepted) and its size in bytes, up to 700 MB. Refused when the line's artwork can no longer change. A chat client that cannot send a file should use attach_artwork_from_url or get_artwork_uploader_link instead. Needs a signed-in Printdash account: called without one, the connection asks the customer to sign in on printdash.io.

content_type.description: Optional; the type is decided by the extension, as the site's uploaders do.

file_name.description: The file's name with its extension: business-card.pdf. PDF is best.

size_bytes.description: The file's size in bytes (up to 700 MB).

design.description: Which design (1 to N) on a job with several designs. Omit on a one-design job.

kind.description: cart_line (line_id from get_cart), quote_line (line_id from get_quote) or order_item (item_id from get_order).

side.description: front (default) or back, on a double-sided job.

name: request_artwork_upload

upload_id.description: Pass to attach_artwork once the PUT succeeded.

upload_url.description: PUT the file's bytes here, with the Content-Type in headers.
